title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
book_title: Chapter 7: Why the Stock Trades Here — Earnout-Adjusted EV, Reverse DCF & Peer Reality

epigraph.quote: Price is what you pay; implied expectations are what you underwrite. When a company adds both bank debt and ₹927 crore of contingent earnouts to buy growth, Enterprise Value tells the truth that trailing P/E hides.
epigraph.author: Institutional Valuation Desk

summary: At ₹1,151.20 on the 25 November 2026 live TradingView snapshot (₹1,160.50 verified 23 November 2026 NSE ledger close), Cyient trades at 33.83x TV / 31.1x Screener TTM earnings and 2.35x book value. Adding ₹2,759 Cr gross borrowings and ₹926.80 Cr TAO Digital contingent earnouts (less ₹587 Cr investments) lifts Earnout-Adjusted EV to ₹15,906 Cr (~23.0x FY26 FCF). Reverse DCF implies ~12.5% 10-year FCF CAGR, pricing in clean DET/TAO/Semi execution with zero margin of safety at CMP.

web_blocks.html: Our price-blind audit in Chapters 1–6 kept Cyient at CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL and PASS_WITH_WATCH [1][4]. We now review the market tape across two verified cutoffs. On the 23 November 2026 NSE ledger, Cyient closed at ₹1,160.50 (+0.43% 1D, +5.19% 1W, +28.51% 3M) [34]. On the 25 November 2026 live TradingView snapshot, shares trade at ₹1,151.20 (-0.80% 1D, +6.52% 1W) after the Nov 18–19 GlobalFoundries $10M CCPS deal [10][28]. Market cap is ₹12,147.35 Cr on TradingView (₹12,807 Cr Screener), 9.85% below its ₹1,277.00 52-week high [1][28].

Headline multiples look rich at 33.83x TradingView TTM P/E (31.1x Screener) and 2.35x book value (₹459/share; 1.39% yield) [1][28]. Trailing EPS fell 34.19% YoY due to FY26 restructuring, ₹71.2 Cr aborted-M&A fees, ₹27.8 Cr goodwill impairment, a ₹46.0 Cr standalone Q2 FX loss, and -₹30 Cr Semi EBIT burn [1][4][14][15][28]. Yet Enterprise Value tells the real story. Adding ₹2,759 Cr gross debt to ₹12,807 Cr equity (less ₹587 Cr investments) yields Standard EV of ₹14,979 Cr (~21.6x FY26 FCF; 14.6x TTM EBITDA) [1]. Adding the ₹926.80 Cr TAO Digital earnout lifts Earnout-Adjusted EV to ₹15,906 Cr (₹15,246 Cr on TV MCap). That equals 23.0x FY26 FCF and 15.5x TTM EBITDA [1][4].

web_blocks.mechanism: Indian ER&D vendors only earn and defend a 30x–35x+ compounder multiple when EBIT margins stay reliably above 15–16%, organic constant-currency growth clears high single digits, and ROCE exceeds 20% on a near-debt-free balance sheet.

web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: Cyient's multiple has already front-run its Semiconductor narrative; sustained re-rating above 26–27x normalized FY28E EPS requires organic DET growth acceleration, Semi breakeven, and visible reduction in combined debt+earnout obligations.

web_blocks.html: Our valuation verdict is clear. After the GlobalFoundries bounce to ₹1,151.20 (₹1,160.50 on 23 Nov ledger), Cyient offers zero margin of safety for fresh cash. Shares trade at 33.83x trailing P/E and ~22.1x–23.0x normalized FY28E EPS (₹50–52) while carrying ~₹3,686 Cr in debt and earnouts. Upside to our ₹1,310.00 Base Target is just +13.8% (+12.9% vs Nov 23 ledger) [4][28][34].

Valuation Trigger: Re-rate Base multiples above 26x FY28E EPS only if Q3/Q4 gross debt drops below ₹2,500 Cr. Semi EBIT losses must also narrow from -₹30 Cr, and DET organic CC growth must top +5% YoY.

book_paragraphs: Now that we have finished our verdict-stripped business audit and Pass 1 blind-spot forensics—retaining a CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL quality rating after uncovering ₹926.80 crore of TAO Digital contingent earnouts, a -₹30 crore quarterly Semiconductor EBIT loss, and continuing C-suite churn—we open the live market screen. Our job in Chapter 7 is simple: separate the excitement around GlobalFoundries' November 18–19 investment from what the share price actually demands in future cash flows.

First, let us keep our two verified price cutoffs completely transparent. On the verified Monday, 23 November 2026 NSE ledger close, Cyient finished at ₹1,160.50 per share (+0.43% on the day, +5.19% over one week, and +28.51% over three months). Two sessions later, on our live 25 November 2026 TradingView snapshot, Cyient trades at ₹1,151.20 (-0.80% on the day, +6.52% over one week), sitting 9.85% below its 52-week high of ₹1,277.00 and 53.4% above its ₹750.30 low. That puts market capitalization at ₹12,147.35 crore on TradingView and ₹12,807 crore on Screener (a gap driven by post-buyback share-count timing), with a trailing P/E of 33.83x on TradingView (31.1x Screener), 2.35x book value (₹459 per share), and a 1.39% dividend yield.

Why is a leveraged ER&D turnaround with 8.61% Screener ROE (6.98% TradingView) and 12.3% ROCE trading above 31x–33x trailing earnings? Two reasons. First, trailing earnings are genuinely depressed (-34.19% TTM EPS YoY) by FY26 restructuring, ₹71.2 crore of aborted-acquisition expenses, ₹27.8 crore of tooling goodwill impairment, a ₹46.0 crore standalone Q2 FX loss, and -₹30 crore of Q2 Semiconductor product R&D losses. Second, the market just re-rated the stock higher on GlobalFoundries' $10 million strategic CCPS investment in Cyient Semiconductors at a $510 million post-money valuation.

Here is where Pass 1 balance-sheet forensics change the valuation math in a way casual headline readers completely miss. Standard Enterprise Value adds ₹2,759 crore of September 2026 gross borrowings to ₹12,807 crore of Screener equity and subtracts ₹587 crore of investments, giving ₹14,979 crore (roughly 21.6x FY26 Free Cash Flow of ₹693 crore and 14.6x TTM EBITDA of ₹1,029 crore). But remember what we uncovered in the Q2 FY27 BSE filing: Other Liabilities jumped ₹1,590 crore to ₹3,727 crore, reflecting ₹926.80 crore of performance-linked contingent earnout obligations for TAO Digital on top of the ₹1,229.50 crore already paid upfront. When you add that ₹926.80 crore debt-like earnout to Enterprise Value, Earnout-Adjusted EV rises to ₹15,906 crore (₹15,246 crore using TradingView's post-buyback market cap)—roughly 23.0x FY26 FCF and 15.5x TTM EBITDA.

Let us run a Reverse Discounted Cash Flow on that ₹15,906 crore Earnout-Adjusted EV using an 11.5% weighted average cost of capital and a 4.5% terminal growth rate. At ₹1,151.20, the market is already pricing in roughly 12.5% annual Free Cash Flow compounding over the next decade. That is not impossible, because FY26 FCF of ₹693 crore predated full-year contributions from TAO Digital and Kinetic Technologies as well as DET's Q2 rebound to a 14.2% EBIT margin. If DET holds 14.0%–14.2% EBIT, TAO and Kinetic integrate cleanly, and Semiconductor losses narrow toward FY28 breakeven, normalized FY28E EPS can reach ₹50–52 per share. Valuing that at 25.5x—a disciplined discount to debt-free LTTS—yields a Base Case fair value of ₹1,310.00 per share (+13.8% vs the ₹1,151.20 live TV close; +12.9% vs the ₹1,160.50 Nov 23 ledger close).

We can cross-check that ₹1,310.00 Base Case with an explicit Sum-of-the-Parts (SOTP) model so we never double-count the Semiconductor headline. Value Cyient DET (including TAO Digital) at 15x FY28E EBIT (~₹965 crore) for ₹14,475 crore; value Cyient's 52.2% stake in listed Cyient DLM at a 20% holding-company discount for ₹1,710 crore; and credit Cyient's ~88% post-CCPS stake in Cyient Semiconductors at GlobalFoundries' $510 million post-money mark (~₹4,300 crore) with an honest 35% discount for the -₹30 crore quarterly EBIT burn, foundry/memory tightness, lack of binding wafer volume, and CCPS liquidation-preference rights—adding ₹2,460 crore. Now subtract ₹3,099 crore of net debt plus TAO contingent earnouts and apply a 10% conglomerate and C-suite-churn discount. You land right around ₹13,991–₹14,570 crore, or ₹1,260–₹1,310 per share. Both earnings and SOTP converge on the exact same answer.

Now check the peer tape on the exact same 25 November 2026 TradingView snapshot. L&T Technology Services (LTTS) trades at ₹4,178.00 (₹44,785.78 crore market cap) and 28.81x TTM P/E with 20.4% TV ROE (26.7% Screener ROCE) and just 0.08x debt-to-equity. KPIT Technologies trades at ₹516.00 (₹14,469.31 crore market cap) and 26.46x TTM P/E with 15.37% TV ROE (26.3% ROCE) and 0.21x D/E. Tata Elxsi trades at ₹3,819.40 (₹23,894.51 crore market cap) and 35.50x TTM P/E with 23.87% TV ROE (60.0% ROCE) and 0.05x D/E. Cyient at 33.83x TTM P/E is priced MORE expensively on trailing earnings than both LTTS and KPIT, despite carrying 0.54x reported debt-to-equity (0.72x with earnouts—already above CRISIL's <0.50x gearing expectation) and less than half their ROCE.

Our independent Chapter 7 takeaway is crystal clear: at ₹1,151.20 (₹1,160.50 on the 23 November ledger), the market has already priced in the GlobalFoundries headline and partial turnaround credit. There is no deep-value cushion here. Fresh capital must demand a much better entry price near structural support—or hard quarterly proof that debt, earnouts, and Semiconductor EBIT losses are all moving in the right direction.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION — Why Contingent Earnouts Belong Inside Enterprise Value
book_callouts.text: When an acquirer pays ₹1,229.50 crore upfront and commits another ₹926.80 crore in performance-linked earnouts for TAO Digital, equity holders do not get the upside for free. If TAO succeeds, Cyient must write large cash checks that compete directly with bank-debt paydown; if TAO misses, Cyient overpaid for the upfront tranche. Putting earnouts into EV keeps our valuation honest.

book_subsections.title: Deconstructing the Earnout-Adjusted Deleveraging Bridge (FY26–FY28E)
paragraphs: In our prior November 13 underwriting, before Pass 1 blind-spot forensics surfaced the ₹926.80 crore TAO Digital earnout liability inside Other Liabilities, the deleveraging math looked deceptively linear: take ₹785 to ₹975 crore of annual Free Cash Flow, pay ₹115 to ₹148 crore of interest and ₹200 crore of dividends, and retire over ₹1,000 crore of bank debt by FY28E. That bridge missed a critical claim on cash.

Once we budget phased TAO Digital earnout settlements alongside moderated dividends (₹350 crore combined in FY27E and ₹490 crore in FY28E) and annualized cash interest of ₹148 crore (reflecting Q2 FY27's ₹37 crore quarterly run-rate stepping down slowly to ₹120 crore), net cash available strictly for bank-debt paydown drops to roughly ₹287 crore in FY27E and ₹365 crore in FY28E. That means consolidated gross borrowings ease from ₹2,759 crore toward roughly ₹2,100 crore by FY28E—not ₹1,750 crore—unless Cyient Semiconductors reaches breakeven ahead of schedule or Cyient DLM rapidly liquidates its 303-day inventory pile.

This also explains why CRISIL's June 9, 2026 rating rationale matters so much. CRISIL explicitly flagged an expectation that Cyient's medium-term gearing would stay below 0.50x. By September 2026, reported borrowings-to-equity had already reached 0.54x—and combined borrowings plus TAO contingent earnouts (~₹3,686 crore) stood near 0.72x equity. Management cannot afford another debt-funded acquisition or a prolonged working-capital squeeze without risking rating pressure and higher borrowing costs.

Now look at the asymmetry between our Bear and Bull cases from this starting balance sheet. In our Bear Case (₹840.00, -27.0% from live TV ₹1,151.20), DET organic constant-currency growth stays stuck near +0.4%, DET EBIT slips back toward 12.5%, Semiconductor quarterly EBIT losses widen past -₹30 crore on foundry and memory bottlenecks, and combined debt plus earnout obligations stay stubbornly above ₹3,400 crore. In that world, EPS stalls near ₹36–38 and the market compresses Cyient to 22–23x earnings (or 13x FCF). Conversely, in our Bull Case (₹1,620.00, +40.7%), GlobalFoundries' strategic partnership translates into commercial ASIC tape-outs that scale Cyient Semiconductors past a $100 million profitable run-rate, DET sustains 15%+ EBIT margins with accelerating organic growth, and the market re-rates Cyient toward 29–30x FY28E EPS of ₹54–55.

book_subsections.title: Peer Hierarchy & Why the GlobalFoundries Mark Is Not a Blank Check
paragraphs: Walk across our verified 25 November 2026 Indian ER&D peer matrix and ask yourself a brutally practical question: if you had ₹1 lakh to deploy into Indian engineering R&D today, why would you pay 33.83x trailing earnings for Cyient when L&T Technology Services (LTTS) is sitting on the exact same screen at 28.81x TTM P/E? LTTS carries a ₹44,785.78 crore market cap, 26.7% Screener ROCE (20.4% TV ROE), 15.47% operating margin, and a fortress 0.08x debt-to-equity ratio—and LTTS is ALSO in a confirmed Stage 2 uptrend.

Tata Elxsi trades at 35.50x TTM P/E—just 1.7 turns above Cyient—while generating 60.0% Screener ROCE, 20.43% operating margins, and 0.05x debt-to-equity. Even KPIT Technologies, currently working through a Stage 4 automotive software reset at ₹516.00, trades at 26.46x TTM P/E with 26.3% ROCE and 0.21x debt-to-equity. Cyient is the ONLY company in this peer group combining sub-13% ROCE, sub-10% TTM operating margin (9.48% TV), and >0.50x leverage.

The single reason the market grants Cyient a 33.83x trailing multiple is optionality: specifically, the hope that Cyient Semiconductors ($510 million post-money valuation following GlobalFoundries' $10 million CCPS check on November 18–19 and EAAA's $30 million check in May 2026) becomes a standalone deep-tech value catalyst. That optionality is real—a Tier-1 foundry like GlobalFoundries does not put its name on a custom ASIC subsidiary lightly. Yet our forensic reading of the BSE Regulation 30 filing forces discipline: there is no disclosed binding wafer-volume commitment, the subsidiary is currently burning -₹30 crore per quarter in EBIT on product R&D, management itself warned of full foundry utilization and memory shortages/costs that could push FY28 breakeven out by one to two quarters, and the Shareholders' Agreement grants GlobalFoundries and EAAA liquidation preference, anti-dilution, reserved-matter consent, and exit rights ahead of common parent shareholders.

Putting it all together, our ₹1,310.00 Base Case target already gives Cyient fair credit for both DET's 14.2% margin turnaround and a risk-adjusted $510 million Semiconductor mark. Paying ₹1,151.20 today for ₹1,310.00 of fair value (+13.8% upside) against ₹970.95 of structural stop-loss risk (-15.7% downside) is an inverted bet. Value discipline says wait for the tape to offer a genuine margin of safety.
